passages.text: Now Ahab told Jezebel everything that Elijah had done and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
passages.sermon:
Ahab was the king of Israel.
Jezebel was his wife.
Elijah was a prophet of the LORD.
Ahab told Jezebel what Elijah had done.
Ahab told her that Elijah had killed all the prophets with the sword.
passages.original: וַיַּגֵּ֤ד אַחְאָב֙ לְאִיזֶ֔בֶל אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרַ֛ג אֶת־ כָּל־ הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

passages.text: So Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, “May the gods deal with me, and ever so severely, if by this time tomorrow I do not make your life like the lives of those you killed!”
passages.sermon:
Jezebel was the queen and the wife of Ahab.
Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah.
The messenger brought a message from Jezebel.
Jezebel said, “May the gods punish me, and punish me even more, if I do not make your life like the life of one of those prophets you killed by this time tomorrow.”
passages.original: וַתִּשְׁלַ֤ח אִיזֶ֙בֶל֙ מַלְאָ֔ךְ אֶל־ אֵלִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּֽה־ יַעֲשׂ֤וּן אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִפ֔וּן כִּֽי־ כָעֵ֤ת מָחָר֙ אָשִׂ֣ים אֶֽת־ נַפְשְׁךָ֔ כְּנֶ֖פֶשׁ אַחַ֥ד מֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And Elijah was afraid and ran for his life. When he came to Beersheba in Judah, he left his servant there, while he himself traveled on a day’s journey into the wilderness. He sat down under a broom tree and prayed that he might die. “I have had enough, LORD,” he said. “Take my life, for I am no better than my fathers.”
passages.sermon:
Elijah was a prophet of God.
Elijah became afraid.
He ran to save his life.
He reached Beersheba, a town in Judah.
He left his servant in Beersheba.
Elijah went alone into the wilderness.
He traveled for one day.
He sat down under a broom tree.
Elijah prayed to die.
He said, “I have had enough, LORD.”
He said, “Take my life.”
He said, “I am no better than my fathers.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֗רְא וַיָּ֙קָם֙ וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ אֶל־ נַפְשׁ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֕א בְּאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֖בַע אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִֽיהוּדָ֑ה וַיַּנַּ֥ח אֶֽת־ נַעֲר֖וֹ שָֽׁם׃ וְהֽוּא־ הָלַ֤ךְ בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ י֔וֹם וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיֵּ֕שֶׁב תַּ֖חַת רֹ֣תֶם אֶחָת וַיִּשְׁאַ֤ל אֶת־ נַפְשׁוֹ֙ לָמ֔וּת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀ רַ֗ב עַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ קַ֣ח נַפְשִׁ֔י כִּֽי־ לֹא־ ט֥וֹב אָנֹכִ֖י מֵאֲבֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: Then he lay down under the broom tree and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”
passages.sermon:
Elijah was a prophet of God.
He was afraid and ran for his life.
He came to the wilderness.
He sat under a broom tree.
He lay down.
He fell asleep.
Suddenly, an angel appeared.
The angel touched Elijah.
The angel spoke to him.
The angel said, "Get up and eat."
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּב֙ וַיִּישַׁ֔ן תַּ֖חַת רֹ֣תֶם אֶחָ֑ד וְהִנֵּֽה־ זֶ֤ה מַלְאָךְ֙ נֹגֵ֣עַ בּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ ק֥וּם אֱכֽוֹל׃

passages.text: And he looked around, and there by his head was a cake of bread baked over hot coals, and a jar of water. So he ate and drank and lay down again.
passages.sermon:
Elijah was a prophet of God.
\r\nElijah was in the wilderness.
\r\nElijah looked around.
\r\nHe saw a cake of bread by his head.
\r\nThe bread was baked over hot coals.
\r\nHe also saw a jar of water.
\r\nElijah ate the bread.
\r\nHe drank the water.
\r\nHe lay down again.
passages.original: וַיַּבֵּ֕ט וְהִנֵּ֧ה מְרַאֲשֹׁתָ֛יו עֻגַ֥ת רְצָפִ֖ים וְצַפַּ֣חַת מָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֣אכַל וַיֵּ֔שְׁתְּ וַיָּ֖שָׁב וַיִּשְׁכָּֽב׃

passages.text: A second time the angel of the LORD returned and touched him, saying, “Get up and eat, or the journey will be too much for you.”
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD came back a second time.
The angel touched Elijah.
The angel spoke to Elijah.
The angel said, “Get up and eat.”
The angel said, “The journey ahead is too much for you.”
passages.original: וַיָּשָׁב֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהוָ֤ה׀ שֵׁנִית֙ וַיִּגַּע־ בּ֔וֹ וַיֹּ֖אמֶר ק֣וּם אֱכֹ֑ל כִּ֛י רַ֥ב מִמְּךָ֖ הַדָּֽרֶךְ׃

passages.text: So he got up and ate and drank. And strengthened by that food, he walked forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.
passages.sermon:
Elijah was a prophet of God.
He got up.
He ate.
He drank.
The food gave Elijah strength.
Elijah walked for forty days.
He walked for forty nights.
He traveled until he reached Horeb.
Horeb is the mountain of God.
passages.original: וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֹּ֣אכַל וַיִּשְׁתֶּ֑ה וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ בְּכֹ֣חַ׀ הָאֲכִילָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה עַ֛ד הַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים חֹרֵֽב׃

passages.text: There Elijah entered a cave and spent the night. And the word of the LORD came to him, saying, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”
passages.sermon:
Elijah was a prophet of the LORD.
Elijah arrived at a cave.
He entered the cave.
He spent the night in the cave.
The word of the LORD came to Elijah.
The LORD spoke to Elijah.
The LORD said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא־ שָׁ֥ם אֶל־ הַמְּעָרָ֖ה וַיָּ֣לֶן שָׁ֑ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה דְבַר־ יְהוָה֙ אֵלָ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מַה־ לְּךָ֥ פֹ֖ה אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts,” he replied, “but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”
passages.sermon:
Elijah was a prophet of the LORD, the God of Hosts.
Elijah spoke to God.
Elijah said, “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts.
The Israelites have abandoned Your covenant.
They have torn down Your altars.
They have killed Your prophets with the sword.
I am the only one left.
They are seeking to take my life.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ קַנֹּ֨א קִנֵּ֜אתִי לַיהוָ֣ה׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֗וֹת כִּֽי־ עָזְב֤וּ בְרִֽיתְךָ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־ מִזְבְּחֹתֶ֣יךָ הָרָ֔סוּ וְאֶת־ נְבִיאֶ֖יךָ הָרְג֣וּ בֶחָ֑רֶב וָֽאִוָּתֵ֤ר אֲנִי֙ לְבַדִּ֔י וַיְבַקְשׁ֥וּ אֶת־ נַפְשִׁ֖י לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then the LORD said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD. Behold, the LORD is about to pass by.” And a great and mighty wind tore into the mountains and shattered the rocks before the LORD, but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Elijah.
The LORD said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD.”
The LORD said, “The LORD is about to pass by.”
A great and mighty wind came.
The wind tore into the mountains.
The wind shattered the rocks before the LORD.
The LORD was not in the wind.
After the wind, there was an earthquake.
The LORD was not in the earthquake.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר צֵ֣א וְעָמַדְתָּ֣ בָהָר֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֒ וְהִנֵּ֧ה יְהוָ֣ה עֹבֵ֗ר וְר֣וּחַ גְּדוֹלָ֡ה וְחָזָ֞ק מְפָרֵק֩ הָרִ֨ים וּמְשַׁבֵּ֤ר סְלָעִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א בָר֖וּחַ יְהוָ֑ה וְאַחַ֤ר הָר֨וּחַ רַ֔עַשׁ לֹ֥א בָרַ֖עַשׁ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: After the earthquake there was a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire came a still, small voice.
passages.sermon: After the earthquake, a fire appeared.\r\nThe LORD was not in the fire.\r\nAfter the fire, a quiet and gentle voice came.
passages.original: וְאַחַ֤ר הָרַ֙עַשׁ֙ אֵ֔שׁ לֹ֥א בָאֵ֖שׁ יְהוָ֑ה וְאַחַ֣ר הָאֵ֔שׁ ק֖וֹל דְּמָמָ֥ה דַקָּֽה׃

passages.text: When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood at the mouth of the cave. Suddenly a voice came to him and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”
passages.sermon:
Elijah was a prophet of the LORD.
Elijah heard a sound.
He wrapped his face in his cloak.
He went out of the cave.
He stood at the entrance of the cave.
A voice came to Elijah.
The voice spoke to Elijah.
The voice said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיָּ֤לֶט פָּנָיו֙ בְּאַדַּרְתּ֔וֹ וַיֵּצֵ֕א וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד פֶּ֣תַח הַמְּעָרָ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ ק֔וֹל וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַה־ לְּךָ֥ פֹ֖ה אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃

passages.text: “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts,” he replied, “but the Israelites have forsaken Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. I am the only one left, and they are seeking my life as well.”
passages.sermon:
Elijah was a prophet of the LORD, the God of Hosts.
Elijah spoke to God.
Elijah said, “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of Hosts.
The Israelites have abandoned Your covenant.
They have torn down Your altars.
They have killed Your prophets with the sword.
I am the only one left.
They are seeking to take my life.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ קַנֹּ֨א קִנֵּ֜אתִי לַיהוָ֣ה׀ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֗וֹת כִּֽי־ עָזְב֤וּ בְרִֽיתְךָ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־ מִזְבְּחֹתֶ֣יךָ הָרָ֔סוּ וְאֶת־ נְבִיאֶ֖יךָ הָרְג֣וּ בֶחָ֑רֶב וָאִוָּתֵ֤ר אֲנִי֙ לְבַדִּ֔י וַיְבַקְשׁ֥וּ אֶת־ נַפְשִׁ֖י לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃ס

passages.text: Then the LORD said to him, “Go back by the way you came, and go to the Desert of Damascus. When you arrive, you are to anoint Hazael as king over Aram.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Elijah.
The LORD gave Elijah a command.
The LORD said, "Go back the way you came."
The LORD told Elijah to travel to the Desert of Damascus.
The LORD said, "When you arrive, anoint Hazael."
The LORD said, "Anoint Hazael as king over Aram."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלָ֔יו לֵ֛ךְ שׁ֥וּב לְדַרְכְּךָ֖ מִדְבַּ֣רָה דַמָּ֑שֶׂק וּבָ֗אתָ וּמָשַׁחְתָּ֧ אֶת־ חֲזָאֵ֛ל לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־ אֲרָֽם׃

passages.text: You are also to anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel and Elisha son of Shaphat from Abel-meholah to succeed you as prophet.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Elijah.
God gave Elijah instructions.
God told Elijah to anoint Jehu.
Jehu is the son of Nimshi.
Jehu will become king over Israel.
God also told Elijah to anoint Elisha.
Elisha is the son of Shaphat.
Elisha is from Abel-meholah.
Elisha will become prophet after Elijah.
passages.original: וְאֵת֙ יֵה֣וּא בֶן־ נִמְשִׁ֔י תִּמְשַׁ֥ח לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאֶת־ אֱלִישָׁ֤ע בֶּן־ שָׁפָט֙ מֵאָבֵ֣ל מְחוֹלָ֔ה תִּמְשַׁ֥ח לְנָבִ֖יא תַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Then Jehu will put to death whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, and Elisha will put to death whoever escapes the sword of Jehu.
passages.sermon:
Jehu is a man chosen by God.
Hazael is a king anointed by God over Aram.
Elisha is a prophet chosen by God to succeed Elijah.
If anyone escapes the sword of Hazael, Jehu will kill that person.
If anyone escapes the sword of Jehu, Elisha will kill that person.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה הַנִּמְלָ֛ט מֵחֶ֥רֶב חֲזָאֵ֖ל יָמִ֣ית יֵה֑וּא וְהַנִּמְלָ֛ט מֵחֶ֥רֶב יֵה֖וּא יָמִ֥ית אֱלִישָֽׁע׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, I have reserved seven thousand in Israel—all whose knees have not bowed to Baal and whose mouths have not kissed him.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Elijah.
God said he would keep seven thousand people in Israel.
These people did not worship Baal.
Their knees never bent to Baal.
Their mouths never kissed Baal.
passages.original: וְהִשְׁאַרְתִּ֥י בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שִׁבְעַ֣ת אֲלָפִ֑ים כָּל־ הַבִּרְכַּ֗יִם אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ כָֽרְעוּ֙ לַבַּ֔עַל וְכָ֨ל־ הַפֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ נָשַׁ֖ק לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So Elijah departed and found Elisha son of Shaphat. He was plowing with twelve teams of oxen, and he was with the twelfth team. Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak around him.
passages.sermon:
Elijah was a prophet of God.
Elijah left that place.
Elijah found Elisha.
Elisha was the son of Shaphat.
Elisha was plowing a field.
There were twelve teams of oxen in front of him.
Elisha was with the twelfth team.
Elijah walked by Elisha.
Elijah threw his cloak over Elisha.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מִ֠שָּׁם וַיִּמְצָ֞א אֶת־ אֱלִישָׁ֤ע בֶּן־ שָׁפָט֙ וְה֣וּא חֹרֵ֔שׁ שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֤ר צְמָדִים֙ לְפָנָ֔יו וְה֖וּא בִּשְׁנֵ֣ים הֶעָשָׂ֑ר וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר אֵלִיָּ֙הוּ֙ אֵלָ֔יו וַיַּשְׁלֵ֥ךְ אַדַּרְתּ֖וֹ אֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: So Elisha left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “Please let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and then I will follow you.” “Go on back,” Elijah replied, “for what have I done to you?”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a farmer.
He worked with oxen in the field.
Elijah was a prophet of God.
Elisha left his oxen.
He ran after Elijah.
Elisha said, “Let me kiss my father and mother goodbye.”
He said, “Then I will follow you.”
Elijah answered him.
Elijah said, “Go back.”
Elijah said, “What have I done to you?”
passages.original: וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב אֶת־ הַבָּקָ֗ר וַיָּ֙רָץ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֵֽלִיָּ֔הוּ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶשְּׁקָה־ נָּא֙ לְאָבִ֣י וּלְאִמִּ֔י וְאֵלְכָ֖ה אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ לֵ֣ךְ שׁ֔וּב כִּ֥י מֶה־ עָשִׂ֖יתִי לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: So Elisha turned back from him, took his pair of oxen, and slaughtered them. With the oxen’s equipment, he cooked the meat and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he set out to follow and serve Elijah.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a farmer.
He had been plowing with oxen.
Elisha turned back from Elijah.
He took his pair of oxen.
He slaughtered the oxen.
He used the oxen’s equipment to cook the meat.
He gave the meat to the people.
The people ate the meat.
Elisha got up.
He followed Elijah.
Elisha served Elijah.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨שָׁב מֵאַחֲרָ֜יו וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־ צֶ֧מֶד הַבָּקָ֣ר וַיִּזְבָּחֵ֗הוּ וּבִכְלִ֤י הַבָּקָר֙ בִּשְּׁלָ֣ם הַבָּשָׂ֔ר וַיִּתֵּ֥ן לָעָ֖ם וַיֹּאכֵ֑לוּ וַיָּ֗קָם וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ אַחֲרֵ֥י אֵלִיָּ֖הוּ וַיְשָׁרְתֵֽהוּ׃פ
